// @path: src/lib/ops/reads.ts
// @expect: OPS-IMPORT-ALLOWLIST
// A real off-allowlist `export … from`, in a file that ALSO contains a string
// literal ending in the word `from`.
//
// The string is the trap and the export is the thing that must still be caught.
// Before F54 the pattern could enter at the string's closing quote and capture
// the code between two literals instead, which meant the genuine specifier on
// the last line was never examined at all. So this fixture asserts the half that
// matters: the real import is still found, with a decoy in front of it.
import { db } from "@/lib/db";

export const note = "a phrase ending in from";
const wherePupilsCome = "the register";

export { sendMail } from "@/lib/mailer";

export async function count() {
  return db.establishment.count();
}
